userStories.title: Ingress trust gate — strict | communication_only | allow_all per channel

Modes: strict (DEFAULT — inbound directives are HELD: create a question-kind row 'Inbound directive awaiting approval' with the message as question_md, subject=the channel row, nothing executes; approving = answering with 'route it'), communication_only (conservative classifier: unconfident ⇒ directive ⇒ held; chatter routes), allow_all (current behavior). userStories.title: CRITICAL — Telegram answer path binds only (workspace,id); an unauthorized chat can inject answers that resume agent work
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (security-reviewer + manual, verified). webhooks.py:243-260 (_find_pending_question, _find_question_by_telegram_message) scope the answer lookup to _pending_questions(workspace_id) ONLY — neither compares the replying Telegram chat against the grant's stored channel_refs.telegram.chat_id (captured at handlers_asks.py:194-202). Telegram delivers EVERY update for the bot token to the one workspace webhook, so any user who can reach the bot (discoverable @username / shared group / ex-member) can (a) reply-collide on the per-chat-sequential reply_to_message_id, or (b) send '/answer <id> <text>' against the global auto-increment ApprovalGrant.id (core/models/approval_grants.py:69) with NO rate limit by default (main.py:865-866 registers SlowAPIMiddleware only when POLICY_PLANE_ENABLED, which config.py:789-798 defaults 'off'). apply_question_answer (api/approval_grants.py:269-294) then flips the grant to GRANTED, appends the attacker text verbatim into the subject's human_qa, and re-dispatches the parked board task (_requeue_blocked_task). Compounding: answered_by is built from reply_ctx['from_user'] = the sender's self-chosen Telegram first_name (webhooks.py:194,322), so the 'human' attribution is itself spoofable (e.g. 'telegram:CEO'). Blast radius is kind='question' rows IN-workspace (the URL webhook_key binds the workspace — NOT cross-workspace). Existing tests cover wrong-workspace and already-answered but NEVER same-workspace-different-chat — the case that matters.

userStories.title: CRITICAL — strict trust gate misses caption / Meta-WhatsApp / edited-message content the router still routes
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (security-reviewer, verified). webhooks.py:354-368 (_inbound_text) reads ONLY message.text, event.text, or top-level text|content|Body; :397-399 treats an empty result as 'nothing to hold (non-text update)' and returns None, so the message falls through to routing REGARDLESS of trigger_mode (including strict). But the router's own ingestor extracts MORE: core/routing/ingestors/webhook.py:54 (Telegram message.caption), :66-73 (Meta-WhatsApp entry[].changes[].value.messages[].text.body), :75-77 (json.dumps(body) fallback). So content the gate scores as empty still becomes envelope.content and reaches UniversalRouter / AutoBrain platform-tool interception (webhooks.py:747-791). Three verified strict-mode bypasses: (1) a connected Meta-WhatsApp channel fails to hold EVERY message (no text/event/Body key); (2) a Telegram photo/document with a caption; (3) a Telegram edited_message (body has 'edited_message', not 'message'). This directly defeats US-006's core guarantee that in strict NOTHING reaches the router for a directive. The trust-gate tests' _tg() helper only ever builds {'message':{'text':..}} — no caption/edited/WhatsApp shape is exercised.

userStories.title: HIGH — blocked cascade ignores OrchestrationTaskDependency edges; returns 0 for the primary mission case
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (code-reviewer + manual, verified). services/ask_cascade.py:4-8 (docstring) claims TWO edge sources — parent_task_id AND the mission OrchestrationTaskDependency DAG — but :51-95 walks ONLY parent_task_id; OrchestrationTaskDependency is never imported or queried anywhere in the PRD. orchestration_board_bridge.py:170-197 makes every mission-step board task a FLAT sibling under one single mission-level parent (parent_task_id = the mission board task), never a child of another step. So the primary real case — an agent executing step N calls platform_ask_human(subject_type='board_task', subject_id=<step N's own board_task id>) — has ZERO parent_task_id children: count_downstream_blocked returns 0 even when steps N+1.. are all blocked on it via OrchestrationTaskDependency. Consequences: US-002's baked urgent-bypass (>=3 dependents) never fires for a genuinely blocking mission ask, and US-004's tab renders an empty cascade. BoardTask.orchestration_task_id (core/models/core.py:1581) is the link to the DAG. No test builds an OrchestrationTaskDependency fixture. userStories.title: MEDIUM — the ingress trust gate fails OPEN on any internal exception
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (security-reviewer, verified). webhooks.py:729-738 wraps _apply_trust_gate in try/except and, on ANY exception, logs and falls through to normal routing (comment: 'routing normally'). A trust gate that fails open silently disables strict for that message on any internal error — a security control one bug away from an unlogged-as-such bypass. (No concrete trigger found today — the internal lookups are isinstance-guarded — so this is a fail-safe-direction correction, not a live exploit.)
acceptanceCriteria: on a gate exception under a non-allow_all channel, the request does NOT reach UniversalRouter or the platform-tool interception — it returns a held/ack response (fail CLOSED) and logs at error level
test: monkeypatch should_hold (or _apply_trust_gate's classify path) to raise; assert the inbound message is not routed

userStories.title: MEDIUM — unauthenticated channel text renders as clickable markdown links in the admin Questions tab
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (security-reviewer, verified). The trust gate embeds RAW inbound text into question_md with no sanitization (webhooks.py:416-420, f-string interpolates text_in.strip()). questions-tab.tsx:101-106 renders question_md via ReactMarkdown + chatMarkdownComponents, whose 'a' renderer (markdown-components.tsx:44-53) passes href straight through (target=_blank). So anyone who can message a strict/communication_only channel gets their raw text — including markdown links like [route it now](https://attacker.example) — stored and displayed as a CLICKABLE link inside the admin's own trusted Questions tab, next to copy priming them to act ('Answer "route it" to let it proceed'). react-markdown without rehype-raw blocks raw HTML/script and strips javascript: URIs, so this is a phishing/social-engineering vector, not proven XSS.
acceptanceCriteria: channel-sourced question_md (trust-gate holds) is stored so the inbound directive text renders as LITERAL text, not active markdown — e.g. the gate fences/escapes the message body so [x](url) and bare autolinks cannot become an anchor
test: a strict-held directive whose body contains [x](https://e.example) produces NO clickable anchor for that inbound text in the rendered card (renders inert)

userStories.title: MEDIUM — a config-only channel update silently drops trigger_mode (reverts to strict)
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (manual, verified). api/channels.py update_channel (~:449-473): when the payload carries 'config' but not 'trigger_mode', new_config = dict(payload['config']) REPLACES the whole config and the stored trigger_mode is not carried over — so trigger_mode_of() reads the default 'strict' on the next read. The code comment (~:452-454) explicitly claims 'a config update never drops the mode', which is false. list_channels (:229) surfaces only trigger_mode (not the raw config, which holds creds), so a client editing credentials cannot round-trip trigger_mode and any creds edit silently resets an operator's allow_all / communication_only choice back to strict. Fail-safe in direction but violates the stated invariant and surprises operators.
acceptanceCriteria: update_channel preserves the existing stored trigger_mode when 'config' is present without an explicit 'trigger_mode' (merge the existing mode into new_config via with_trigger_mode from the row's current config), unless the caller explicitly sets a new mode
test: PUT {config:{bot_token:'x'}} against a channel whose stored config has trigger_mode='allow_all' leaves trigger_mode 'allow_all' afterward

userStories.title: MEDIUM — platform_ask_human reports parked:true for a terminal subject that can never resume
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (code-reviewer, verified). handlers_asks.py:94 skips the block-flip when the board task is already terminal (status in done/failed — _PARKED_STATUSES), but :116-127 still creates the question grant and unconditionally returns {success:True, parked:True, message:'Parked ...'}. Answering that question later no-ops the resume — _requeue_blocked_task only acts if task.status=='blocked' (api/approval_grants.py:385) — yet the grant still flips to GRANTED and _confirm_answer_into_chat (api/approval_grants.py:326-344) tells the human the work is 'resuming'. The tool lies about parking and the human is told resumption happened when it did not.
acceptanceCriteria: when the board_task subject is terminal (done/failed/cancelled) at ask time, ask_human returns success:False (or parked:False) with an honest message and does NOT create a resumable question row or emit a 'Parked ...' confirmation
test: ask_human against a done board task returns parked False (or an error) and does not fabricate a Parked message
